q: Does an ice bank or chilled water storage tank cut my Scope 2 emissions?
title: Thermal storage and Scope 2
short: Usually not on the location-based method. Storage shifts chiller load to night, but India's grid factor is one annual average (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so the same kWh give the same CO2. Making ice can even use more kWh. It can still cut cost and peak demand.
audience: Facility managers, cold chain and process cooling users

ul: If storage lets you use more of your own solar output.
Under the market-based method, if a contract supplies renewable power at the hours you charge.
If it lets a chiller run at its best load instead of cycling.
Ice making runs chillers at lower temperatures, so efficiency drops.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
